column8: Thu 19 Nov: twin of H3-050 (Ulysses at the mast, textbook); the plea-refused rule is l.17's bright line already in Q7b-028; the picture stays out (Q7b-042), and the rope-tightens gloss adds nothing CONCEIT 3b's ink only goes one way lacks.

Thu 19 Nov: store, idea 1's support: the tie has its own end date, as each rung matures just before its payment (l.13); plain words only unless the lead reopens Q7b-042; the break (untied when the danger passed, a Treasury ends by contract) sits with Q166's date-not-danger rows.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 or 3c in plain words, the heart of idea 1: a rule is an oath that holds only while keeping it is cheap, so the plan states no figure that needs one through a long bad spell; NUMBERS 8p checked ($95,000-$105,000, bottom and payments unchanged); plain-words twin of Q7b-034, the oath-and-rope pairing is the new part; the Odyssey stays out unless the lead reopens Q7b-042.
Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 support: ink needs nobody awake; keep the break in any use, Table 3 still watches an early end or merger of a fund, so never no monitoring; on tour is an image, not a case fact.
Thu 19 Nov: store only: the shape of a breach now, repaid later, which l.13 refuses; nobody in the plan argues for selling, so it serves no live decision; never imply the team would sell.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3e support: the tie is on money, not on Laura, which answers the self-control misreading (Q7b-028); the crew outvoting him first (12.297) makes the oath a second best, so say device, not character; picture out unless Q7b-042 reopens.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c support for row 8: one date can ruin a plan, the first plan's one date (8s) and the rival's 16.4% under $95,000 (8c), both checked; never 3.2% fails high; Charybdis has no middle and markets do.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, the one image that maps a register figure line for line: the bottom bought in January 2028 is a smaller toll paid in most worlds against a timing gamble; 8c checked ($7,400, 59.8%, 68.4%, $105,843 against $22,573 from July 1929); the toll is a smaller middle, never a loss of anything stated; needs the lead to reopen Q7b-042.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e wording support only: state 8c's price because no stated figure rests on anyone's nerve; two ideas in one row (hiding the cost, acting in the moment), so split before use; no trading in a stress is card Q45's.
Thu 19 Nov: store: pull to par in an image, a textbook bond fact; the image stays out (Q7b-042) and an iBond fund's payout is never fixed.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b and 3c, idea 3: Strotz's two answers split by money, promised money tied now and the 2031 move a plan she will want to follow because she can name only an owned top; it answers Elster's warning, a binding mistake lands only on pencil (8c's $7,400, 8p and NUMBERS 3's $4,589 checked); new beside H3-049 and H4-143, which name Strotz only.
Thu 19 Nov: 3c support for row 11 and H2-052; keep its honest limit, the rule to state only owned money is itself an oath held by credibility (case p.3), never forced.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3e, one clause: binding the payments costs Laura nothing beyond owning the Treasuries, so the plan's price of commitment is 8c's about $7,400 middle (checked); the opportunity cost of Treasuries against shares stays the price of certainty, never of the tie.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b support (half the shares as a partial rule, row 11's domain of discretion); the quote is from NBER WP 208 (rev. 1978), so cite the working paper or read the 1981 JPE text before citing it; never imply Laura doubts her willpower.
Thu 19 Nov: store: a pedigree line that only marks the disanalogy (her tie answers an income that falls with markets, l.9, not self-control); half a clause beside row 11 at most.

Thu 19 Nov: store, Elster's ladder mapped loosely: a Treasury's price still shows on a screen, so held to the end means no decision rests on it, not that the occasion is avoided; Q7b-027 and Q7b-034 carry the stronger form.
Thu 19 Nov: a guard (dated steps for the plan, binding only for the move); the same point as Q7b-034, before 2031 nothing binds the plan in Elster's strict sense.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Daniel 6 not read, so read it before any use; the no-exit law is a wording contrast only, and Q164's saving clause is the fuller home for why the plan keeps two narrow exits.

Thu 19 Nov: UNVERIFIED, read only in Rothwell's thesis: read Elster 1979 p.36 and 2000 p.90 at source before use; the point (a fully rational founder would also want her figure in ink) adds little to Q7-002 and Q7-015.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or 2.2, two ideas to split: the binding written in calm on the case's dates against triggers that bind after markets move, and 8e's history (0% of 2010s days, $470,217 on 4 Aug 2020, both checked); keep the flag, 8e is history, never a forecast.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c support: the bottom bought three years before the meetings and the top moved on 1 January 2031 (8r, checked) build in the delay Elster and Kydland and Prescott prescribe; their delay guards the rule-maker's passions, Laura's the market's timing, so say which.
Thu 19 Nov: pedigree, the store's H7-058 (rules beat discretion when others plan around your word); the not stupid or evil quote may join it.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, idea 4's hook: IPS l.17 has the shape of a British statute, fixed dates and exactly two named exits; a finance judge will not know it; the break (votes there, events here) is the lesson in rows 24-26.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, the aha: exits the bound party can vote become the decision, while Laura's are checked on paper, and a rewrite cannot reach money already in Treasuries unless she sells; fix the wording, a missed deposit is not wholly nobody's choice, so say the one exit she could cause closes by 31 March 2028 (8u, checked), before anyone relies on a figure.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, one clause: exits held by words gave one full term and the Act was repealed; Laura's stated figures rest on owned Treasuries, so the plan's weakest part carries no promise; never only two things can break the plan (Q109).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, the line a rule is only as strong as what holds it (two reasons in a letter, figures in Treasuries); fix: Elster named the flaw in 1995 about Poland's court, so never say he foresaw the Act.
Thu 19 Nov: store: marks a disanalogy only (known dates help a politician's rivals, while co-sponsors plan around Laura's); no decision changes.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.2 support for GOLDMINE 27's dated steps: date locks arrived, amount locks rarely did; resolve 140 against 147 (pp. 639, 657) or say most, and keep the break, a date lock arrives by itself, which is the point, not proof of willpower.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, one clause: exits that need a document went unused, as l.17's two are checked on a bank record or a Treasury payment record (Q7b-028); six months at one bank is thin, so never rarely used in general.
Thu 19 Nov: store, colour for l.13's just before it is needed; the 7-9 days before 1 January is store row Q138-041's arithmetic, not in NUMBERS, so book it there before any use.

Thu 19 Nov: store: stating a missed deposit's consequence in advance is old practice, and l.13's order (complete the ladder first) is the plan's version; the club punished the saver, the plan only reorders purchases.
Thu 19 Nov: the same point as row 13 (the tie costs Laura no interest; clubs cost savers theirs); the Library of Congress quote may join row 13.
Thu 19 Nov: a citation guard; Q7-014 already bars Ariely and Wertenbroch, and the retraction's reason may be added there.
Thu 19 Nov: a wording ban (never burned his boats): the famous binding bound others under a pretext, Q7-015's point; Laura's tie is open, in a letter to the person whose money it is.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3.0, a far-field aha from Taiwan's own idiom dictionary: famous ties bet everything forward, Laura's takes promised money out of risk, and the 2031 move in a good January is the opposite idiom, stepping bravely back from a strong current (the temptation H2-052 names); never in Laura's words to co-sponsors.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e's lead, the synthesis: rescues from Athens to Goschen moved the date, the thing paid or the rule; fix two things: the card's own rows 3 and 31 (a tax, a levy) show a fourth lever, more money from others, which l.11 removes, so the instruments take two, l.11 a third, and l.17 writes down the rule; and an iBond fund can end early and pays its value, never a fixed sum, so never cannot move (NUMBERS 3, Table 3 row 4); the ways to fail stay a separate list (Q109).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 2.0, the plan's own rule seen from its failure side: Rome voted the sums in 5 CE and found the money in 6 CE, while Laura owns first and states second (l.15); with rows 4-5 it shows what follows when the order is reversed.
Thu 19 Nov: 3d support for SD-3: the founder's own money first, then others'; the 14,167 (Keel arithmetic) needs no place in the report; never the largest share, never nearly sixfold for Laura.
Thu 19 Nov: store and row 1's evidence: paid late and in something else, the two levers dated Treasuries take away; Tacitus wrote a century later, a grievance, not an audit.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, a third term for Q153-042's contrast (firms hold back the size, Rome the payment's date, Laura the day she states); one outside name per part (panel 4), so Lintner or Rome, not both; never say nobody can move a date (a fund can end early).

Thu 19 Nov: 3a, why a closed set of payments can be bought outright while an endless one needs a flow; fix: the case sets the ten payments (case p.2), not the IPS, so never why the IPS names ten payments.
Thu 19 Nov: 3e setup for row 8: a guarded reserve with a named exit, the design of l.17; Athens guarded a danger, Laura's reserve guards ten dates.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e and 3b, the aha: a 19-year test of an exit rule, which fell when a panic had no other money; Laura's half kept gives a building panic its own money (l.15), so nothing pushes on the rule that guards the payments; keep the break (Chios brought the named danger closer).

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0, a fact for certainty has dates: a reserve kept for a purpose can be argued away by declaring the purpose done, one kept for a date cannot; force also opened Caesar's door, so say argument and force.
Thu 19 Nov: store: textbook, and Joseph stored by a rule (a fifth), not to a sum; colour only.
Thu 19 Nov: the same test as H4-008 (who holds the money); held for her is UCC 8-503's word, never identified.

Thu 19 Nov: store, one clause in 3a at most: the closest ancestor of a fixed sum on a date, read at source, so it supersedes H4-035 and H5-105's description; 11.3% and 13.0% rechecked (Keel arithmetic); the high rates lean on forfeits, the disanalogy worth keeping.

Thu 19 Nov: corrects store row H4-035 (a raid in the 1480s) to 1452 at source (Kirshner and Molho 1978, p. 438, n. 65), so the lead fixes H4-035's date; the circularity lesson itself is Q62-040 and Q62-041's.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c wording with a fact behind it: Florence called its own debt immovable rock in 1470 and capped payouts in 1477, so certain takes the stated range as its subject; keep the honest break, the US is also a payer that sets its own rules, so the difference is a dated bond owned by a third party, never words against no words.
Thu 19 Nov: 3d support: a co-sponsor counts a figure by its date as well as its size (the groom would not wait to 1448), l.13's matching seen from the receiver's side; the Italian original is unseen.

Thu 19 Nov: the mapping turns on itself: the US's long record is a record too, so a record is pencil invites the judge's obvious reply; use Venice only for row 19's point (a promise with no date leaves the date to the payer) or drop it.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.2 or 3a, one clause: holding to the end needs an end (the Monte Vecchio had none, its bonds near 5 by 1500), history for l.13 and for H8-032 and H9-057; never an iBond fund's payout as fixed.
Thu 19 Nov: store and row 1's evidence: a payer holding a call keeps the letter and pays less; no callable Treasury issued since 1985 (Q104-022), so her bonds leave no such option.
Thu 19 Nov: store: an undated promise leaves the date to the payer; pairs with row 17, one of the two at most.
Thu 19 Nov: 3b support: building money kept apart from running money has 1,500 years of pedigree, the split l.11 and l.15 make; a quarter share is not a sum sized to a building.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Exeter's restricted Fabric Fund is pedigree for keeping building money apart; colour beside row 20, one of them at most.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b, a strikingly dissimilar parallel: services ran in Cologne's choir while the towers waited, as the ten payments run while the building stays pencil; keep the break (a residency cannot run in half a building, so her flexibility, not time, does the waiting); read the 1322 choir date at source.
Thu 19 Nov: 3d store: co-sponsors finish what a founder has visibly begun, and one still pays about 60% of the yearly budget; the king was not the founder, so it never shows the founder pays first.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b, the Facciatone shows a building promised before its money is owned; fix: the vote count conflicts (132 or 172 against), so drop it, and say the plague and the building's faults stopped the work, not money alone.
Thu 19 Nov: store, colour for the closing line (risk on the page, none with the promises); one outside name per part, none in 3f.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d support: a co-sponsor's oldest question is the founder's own money, which is why Laura's own figure comes first; indulgences are nothing like a co-sponsor's grant, so one clause at most.
Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3e: a figure with an if in its sentence is pencil, whatever its arithmetic; pairs with row 28, which carries the outcome.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e and 3b: Franklin's arithmetic held and his engine faded, so a forecast is fine for money promised to no one (her flexibility) and the top is moved before it is stated; fix: say about two-thirds (67% against 69% conflict) and Philadelphia about a fifth.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e support: a fixed charge against a growing cost runs short, as building costs grow while the contribution is a stated range (+7.18%, 8d, checked); fix: the about 25% cover holds if shares earn the 7.5% assumed (23.6% at 6.5%, 8u), and the $50,000 payments buy less each year too (8d), so never imply inking escapes inflation.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a support for NUMBERS 2's standard (sufficient without reinvestment): a promise valued on an assumed rate moved when rates moved; whether the societies failed is contested (Broten), so use the valuation fact only.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3e, the lever Laura gave up: societies survived short years by levying members, and l.11 says no payment depends on anybody else's money, so hers must be owned before it is stated; the fourth lever row 1 must add.
Thu 19 Nov: store: marks a disanalogy only (pooling many lives against one founder and ten dates); the 1-pound story is disputed (Dunlop's about 5%, unread), so never the 1-pound figure alone.
